name: Comal Oculto
description: Michelin Bib Gourmand spot in San Miguel Chapultepec built around the comal, with one long communal table. Michelin singles out the gordita especial. Open only a few days a week at lunch, so check before going.
special_quality: A Bib Gourmand comal counter where the gordita especial is the draw.
address: Protasio Tagle 66A, San Miguel Chapultepec (a third-party listing gives Manuel Gómez Pedraza 37; verify)

name: Tamales Doña Emi
description: Family tamal stand that began as a cart in the 1960s, now run by the founder's granddaughter. Big, fluffy, moist tamales in classic (verde, mole, rajas) and modern flavors like huitlacoche with goat cheese and frijol with chapulines. Order a guajolota (tamal in a bolillo) with atole; they sell out by midday.
special_quality: The Roma tamal institution, with 60-plus years of family history and a mod menu next to the classics.
address: Jalapa s/n (about no. 277-278), esq. Tlaxcala, Roma Sur; Tue-Sun mornings (verify)

name: Tortas Armando
description: Claims to trace to 1892, when Armando Martínez Centurión sold tortas from a portal in the Centro. More than 20 varieties, from jamón y queso to pastor and chilaquiles. Two branches (Cuauhtémoc and Del Valle).
special_quality: One of the oldest continuously operating tortas brands in the city, claiming 1892.
address: Río Nazas 64, Cuauhtémoc; also Pedro Romero de Terreros 201, Del Valle

name: La Casa del Pavo
description: Century-old Centro tortería, reported opened in 1901 on Motolinía, famous for its turkey torta (turkey bought at La Merced, prepared a la vinagreta and griddled) and a bacalao torta. It appears in Cuarón's Roma and is tied to the torta cubana origin story. A 2015 column reported a closure, but 2023-2025 pieces describe it as open; verify.
special_quality: Turkey torta from a 1901 counter, with a film cameo and a disputed role in inventing the cubana.
address: Motolinía 40, Centro Histórico (verify current status)

special_quality: Chilaquil-and-milanesa torta from a family stall on a Condesa corner.

special_quality: Rectangular Zacatlán-style tlacoyos with arvejón, which are rare in the city.
